title: MBIM: Dissect MBIM_CID_MS_VOICE_EXTENSIONS_NITZ
description: This change enables the dissection of the command - MBIM_CID_MS_VOICE_EXTENSIONS_NITZ.

notes.body: The filter is still named mbim.control.device_caps_info.data_class which is not relevant for your new dissection. I suggest you to leave this one as is and create a new one
Are you ok with this update per our discussion of hf_mbim_year?
No I'm not especially as the filter name has not changed.

You are right. What I mean to say is "are you ok to update it to hf_mbim_data_class so it can be shared by different commands". I will update its filter name to mbim.control.data\_class if you agree it.
After more thoughts, I do not think it is a good idea to change a long exiting filter name a it might break other people workflow.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/11719/diffs?diff_id=765048048&start_sha=57afad6cd48583ac583f6cc1f63bda8d9bea7bca#3f4c602f6670690382c1b302509061e51de0a1de_141_143)
Why is this filter (and the following ones) prefixes with this generic mbim.control name?

I want to make those filter as generic so it can be shared by different commands in the future. That is also why I change hf_mbim_device_caps_info_data_class to `hf_mbim_data_class` since they look exactly the same in different commands for less code and better performance purpose. If you insist they should be separated, I can separate them in next iteration.

For your consideration, my personal Wireshark usage experience is separating them won't improve my personal user experience since it is impossible to remember so many filters. And one benefit to share them is most of those commands sharing the same filter are relevant, it probably is more useful to share the same filter if the data itself has the same meaning so those relevant commands will be displayed when I use the same filter.

So far the mbim dissector rules was to have filters with the command included and then the parameters so that when you filter you can ensure you do not get extra unrelated messages. But I see your point also. I guess there is no perfect answer as it mostly depend on how you use Wireshark. To be honest I stopped using MBIM years ago and I'm no more an active user. But what makes toubthinog those fields that are really specific to NITZ will ever by used for something else? Why control rather than nitz?

Up till now, no other control has those fields. I make it common in case it may be needed by new controls added in the future. I can update this to nitz specific in next iteration if you are not convinced.
I can bet that no other command will use the same fields
